title: Coherent ordinary scalar-extension copowers and exactness
statement: Fix a prime ell and a finite intermediate field E of its algebraic closure Omega, with the internal condensed modules of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] and scalar actions of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-derived-scalar-basis-pushforward]. There exist a common index type I and coefficient sections b(Z,i):1 -> Omega_Z for every scheme Z, coherent under pullback along every scheme morphism. Extension from E_Z to Omega_Z preserves finite limits. For each ordinary E_Z-module N and any chosen I-copower of N, the coproduct of the ordinary extension adjunction unit followed by restricted multiplication by b(Z,i) is an isomorphism to the restriction of its ordinary scalar extension. No derived-category isomorphism is assumed.

proof.text: Apply exists_padicAlgCl_point_basis: the uniform finite-support coordinate construction gives a small-indexed coproduct of regular finite coefficient modules isomorphic to the restricted regular algebraic closure module on the profinite point. This construction is proved, including its sheafification transport.

For arbitrary commutative ring objects R -> S on the profinite point with this coproduct decomposition, map the regular modules and the coproduct through the point inverse image to every scheme. The module functor preserves coproducts: after its conservative forgetful functor this is the colimit preservation of the left-adjoint geometric inverse image. Define each basis section by pulling back the corresponding point section. The monoidal composition comparison in profinite_point_pullback proves coherence. Keeping this construction generic in R and S avoids expensive conversion through the concrete finite-subextension coefficient objects.

Tensor the pulled-back regular-module coproduct with an arbitrary module N. The left unitor, tensor coproduct comparison, and scalar-extension tensor comparison give an isomorphism from the chosen coproduct of N to the restriction of its scalar extension. The extension-unit/scalar-action calculation identifies every coproduct leg with exactly the displayed adjunction unit followed by restricted qbar_scalarEndo. The proof specifies the constant N diagram explicitly, so works for every chosen HasCoproduct instance. Finally the regular module is the tensor unit and is flat; coproducts preserve flatness. Transport flatness along the decomposition, use extendForgetTensorIso, and reflect finite-limit preservation along the exact conservative forgetful functor.

proof_origin.place: The proved generic scheme_basis_from_point construction, its scalar-unit leg computation and flatness argument, instantiated with the proved point basis.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_condensedQbar_scalar_basis_sections :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1))
      (b : ∀ Z : Scheme.{u}, I →
        (𝟙_ (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z) Ab.{u + 1}) ⟶
          condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) Z)),
      (∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : I), b X i =
        Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (f)^*[Ab.{u + 1}] ≫
          (f)^*[Ab.{u + 1}].map (b Y i) ≫
            condensedPullbackHom (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) f) ∧
      (∀ Z : Scheme.{u}, PreservesFiniteLimits (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap
        (Profinite.padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl ℓ E) Z))) ∧
      (∀ (Z : Scheme.{u})
        (N : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z) Ab.{u + 1})
          (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) Z))
        [HasCoproduct (fun _ : I ↦ N)],
        IsIso (Sigma.desc (f := fun _ : I ↦ N) fun i ↦
          (Mod.extendRestrictAdjunction (coefficientMap
            (Profinite.padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl ℓ E) Z)).unit.app N ≫
          (Mod.comap (coefficientMap
            (Profinite.padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl ℓ E) Z)).map
            (Mod.qbar_scalarEndo (b Z i) ((Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap
              (Profinite.padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl ℓ E) Z)).obj N))))

mathlib_searches.query: Restriction of the condensed regular algebraic closure to a finite p-adic extension is a direct sum of copies of the regular module, indexed by a vector-space basis, because finite-extension-valued continuous functions have finitely many continuous coordinates
mathlib_searches.results: 8 hits, including LocallyConstant.freeOfProfinite, p-adic complex scalar algebra and Condensed.finFree. No finite-subextension-valued condensed coefficient basis or ordinary extension-unit theorem.
